The annotation library allows you to save annotations or groups of annotations for reuse in other Documents or other Projects.

Open the library from the toolbar with the button. You can select: Recently used annotations. The User annotations that you imported into the library. Media: images or videos imported into the Project that you can use as annotations. The different categories of annotations.

Annotations added to the library are available for all projects. Select an annotation in the main view of a Document. Use Add to User Library in the selected annotation’s actions. The annotation is added to the User category of the library. You can delete an annotation added to the library: Tap the icon at the top right of the annotation.
documents.s: Add an annotation to the library

documents.t: Annotations are graphics, text, images or videos that you can add to Documents. You cannot add annotations directly to files; you must create a Document to use the annotations.

First place the playhead at the time position where the annotation should appear. Open the annotation library with the button on the toolbar. Select a category and an annotation. The annotation appears in the main view. In a Representation Document, if the playhead is outside the visible area of the main view, the annotation is added at the center of the view.

When you add a line, polygon or Bézier shape annotation, no annotation is added immediately to the main view: Tap to add points: 2 for lines and 3 or more for polygons and Bézier shapes. Double-tap the final point. The annotation then appears in the main view.

When you add a drawing annotation, no annotation is added immediately to the main view: Draw directly in the main view with Apple Pencil or your finger. When you finish drawing, the annotation is added. On iPadOS, drawings use PencilKit. See Drawing with PencilKit for details.

Cursors are somewhat special annotations: they appear in the form of animated graphics based on keyframes. They are used to create playheads that move on a score to the rhythm of the music or annotations that highlight the sequence of several notes or chords. Cursors can only be created in Slideshow Documents. There are four types of cursors: : horizontal scrolling. : vertical scrolling. : circular scrolling. : scrolling following a line. You can add multiple cursors to each slide. There are two techniques for adding cursors: Manual: you adjust each keyframe manually. This is ideal for creating a playhead on a slightly complex score or one that has tempo variations. Easy: you adjust the time synchronization during playback. This technique is ideal for scores at a moderate tempo in which there are no tempo variations.

Position the playhead at the moment where the cursor should appear. Tap the button on the toolbar and choose Add Manual Cursor. In the window that opens, choose the cursor properties: Its Type. Its Shape. Not all shapes are available for all types. The number of Keyframes: you can add or delete keyframes later. This number includes the first and last keyframes at the ends of the cursor. Whether the position of the shape should be Interpolated between keyframes. The Color. Tap Add. You cannot change the Type of a cursor once it is added. With the exception of Type, all of these properties can then be edited with the Property inspector.

Position the playhead at the moment where the cursor should appear. Tap the button on the toolbar and choose Add Easy Cursor. The left sidebar opens and allows you to manage the steps: Step 1: mark the graphical positions. Tap the main view to position the keyframes, for example on the beats of the score inserted as the slide background. You can change the cursor's Size and Color in the left sidebar. Step 2: Tap Time-based positions in the left sidebar. Start playback and tap on the main view to associate a time position with each graphic position. Step 3: Tap Finalize in the left sidebar. The cursor is created on the main view.

Select the cursor and open the inspector with the toolbar button to display its properties in the left sidebar. Specific cursor properties can be found in the tab: Modify the Shape. Not all shapes are available for all types. Change the Direction of the triangular shape. Enable or disable Interpolation between keyframes. Keyframe Animation: apply annotation animation to each keyframe. Smoothing: smoothes the line for type cursors. Width of certain cursor types. Size of certain cursor types. Center size of type cursors. Path: only for types : Visible: display the line followed by the cursor. Hide shape. Size of the shape. Selected Frame: this is the keyframe currently displayed in the main view: Last Frame: display the properties of the last keyframe. Interpolation: interpolate with the next keyframe. Position between 0.0 and 1.0. Time. Color. Opacity.
Select the cursor and use Delete in the editing actions.

To change a cursor's keyframes: Double-tap it; the cursor switches to advanced editing mode. You can change the position of a keyframe in the main view by taping and dragging the corresponding handle Tap between two keyframes to add a keyframe. Touch and hold a keyframe to open its context menu, then choose the delete command. In the timeline, keyframes appear as vertical lines: Touch and drag a keyframe. You cannot delete or add keyframes in the timeline; you must do it in the main view.
You can edit the properties of an annotation in several ways.

Tap the annotation and change its position or size using the selection handles. If the annotation is a line, you can move it using its handles at both ends. If the annotation is a polygon or Bézier shape, double-tap to edit the points: Touch and drag the point handles. Touch the position between two points and use to add a new point. Use the delete command shown on a point when available. You can also select multiple annotations to move or resize them together: Touch outside the annotations and drag to select multiple annotations. Edit the bounding box that contains the selected annotations.
When an annotation is selected in the main view, a rectangle appears in the timeline: Touch the start, center or end. Draggable areas appear in the accent color. Drag to change the time properties.
Open the inspector with the button on the toolbar to modify all the properties. On iPadOS, the inspector appears in the left sidebar.
Open the inspector with the toolbar button, then use the tab to edit the annotation animations. You can add entry, exit, and content animations.
When you modify the temporal properties of an object, you have 2 possibilities: Editing by units by touch. Manual editing.
Tap one of the units (minutes:seconds:milliseconds). The unit is selected. Drag up or down to cycle through values by +/-1.
Double-tap to enter the time value using the syntax: 00:00.000 (minutes:seconds:milliseconds). The syntax must be exact (number of digits, position of : and .) for the value to be taken into account.
Select the annotation and use Delete in the editing actions.

Layers allow you to organize the annotations of a Document. They are useful for separating multiple levels of analysis, displaying only certain annotations, or controlling their behavior during playback.

Each annotation belongs to a layer. A Project can use as many layers as you want. For example, you can use one layer for general comments, another for musical elements, and another for visual cues, etc.

To display the layer editing interface, use the last tab of the Document properties in the left sidebar. You can also edit a layer from an annotation with the button located to the right of the drop-down menu allowing you to choose the layer.
Select a layer from the top list. Use the button to add a layer. Use the button to delete a layer.

In the layers list, you can: Use the button to hide or show the layer annotations. Use the button to lock the layer annotations. In this case, you can no longer edit their graphic or temporal position in the main view and the timeline, but the inspector properties remain available. You can also use the controls below the list: Modify the Title of the layer. Visible: show or hide the layer annotations. Locked: lock the graphic and temporal editing of layer annotations.
documents.s: Show, hide or lock a layer

documents.t: Layers can control how annotations appear during playback. Depending on the settings, annotations can follow their temporal duration, maintain a common color or opacity, or take on a different appearance outside of their active duration. Select a layer from the list: the properties are displayed below. Time Animation: track the start and end temporal properties of annotations to determine their display. Mode: Start and Stay: Once the layer annotations appear, they remain displayed. Continuous: the layer's annotations always remain displayed, and you can modify their color and opacity outside their time range with the two properties below. Color: color annotations outside their time range. Opacity: change the opacity of annotations outside their time range. Layers in Representation Documents default to Mode > Continuous.

With iAnalyse, you work from imported files by creating Documents. There are 4 types of Documents: Slideshow, to prepare a simple presentation, annotate a score or any other use in which you need several pages. Representation, to work with temporal or graphic visualizations. Video, to work with video media. Canvas, to freely organize objects and annotations on a view. On iPadOS, Documents follow the same principles as on macOS. The main differences are access to properties in the left sidebar and touch interactions in the main view.

To create a Document, first select an audiovisual or music file (MIDI, MusicXML, or MEI). Use the add button or the creation menu, then choose one of the available Document types. Video Documents can only be created from a file with a video track.

Documents include 2 elements: The editing view, which occupies the largest area: it is the view which will be exported, for example as an image or video. The timeline under the editing view: it displays the temporal properties of the elements selected in the editing view.
The grid appears on the editing view. Depending on the Documents, it can take several forms.

The regular grid is present in Slideshow, Video and Canvas Documents. It is managed by 5 properties: Visibility. Magnetism for annotations. Mode: grid or points. The spacing determines the size of the grid. Divisions determines the number of subdivisions of the grid.

In the representations, the grid and the vertical rulerr are combined and the properties are distributed over two panels. The representation properties inspector provides access to general properties: Display allows you to display the time ruler, vertical rulerr and grid. Target determines the representation that will be used to construct the vertical rulerr and the grid. Mode determines the vertical ruler to use for musical representations (logarithmic spectrogram, fundamental frequency, etc.): frequencies or musical pitches. To display the vertical rulerr and horizontal grid lines, you must select a representation in the Target property. The advanced properties panel is displayed by tapping the button. Advanced properties: grid: Set the display of the vertical and horizontal lines of the grid. Color of the grid. Opacity of the grid. Mode determines the ruler to use for musical representations (logarithmic spectrogram, fundamental frequency, etc.): frequencies or musical pitches. Advanced properties: pitch graduations: These controls are only active if a musical representation is selected in Target and Pitch is selected in Mode. A3 Frequency: the reference tuning frequency. Element: the line of the note to edit. Visibility [grid and ruler]: display of the note. Octave [ruler]: display of the octave number. Min. Range and Max. Range [grid and ruler]: allow you to reduce the displayed pitch range. Color [grid and ruler]. Line [grid]: thicker or dotted line. Pitch parameters are only active with representations based on logarithmic frequency visualization or musical pitch extraction.
A Canvas Document displays a resizable graphic space on which you can add annotations.

After selecting a Document, display the Property inspector with the button on the toolbar. On iPadOS, the inspector appears in the left sidebar. The Property inspector contains several tabs: The general properties of the canvas: this is the first tab. The annotation layer properties.

The title of the canvas as it appears in the browser. The width of the canvas. The height of the canvas. In the background properties, the mode displays the 3 possibilities: color depending on the system interface (light or dark), choice of a specific color, choice of an imported image (import the image so that it is available in the list). The grid properties.
A Slideshow Document consists of slides in which you can insert a background image and annotations.
Position the playhead in the timeline where you want to add the slide. Select the button from the toolbar. Tap Add Slide.

Open the Property inspector by tapping the button on the toolbar. Edit the properties of the Slide. You can also edit the time position of the slide in the timeline: Touch the start of the slide in the timeline. The selection bar appears in color. Drag the selection bar. The Slide part of the inspector displays the properties of the slide displayed in the main view. Use the Timeline playhead to change the displayed slide.
Show the slide to be deleted in the main view. Use Delete in the editing actions or the delete command in the context menu. The first slide cannot be deleted.

After selecting a Document, display the Property inspector with the button on the toolbar. On iPadOS, the inspector appears in the left sidebar. The Property inspector contains several tabs: The general properties of the slideshow: this is the first tab. The annotation layer properties.

The title of the slideshow as it appears in the browser. The ratio determines the size of the slideshow slides. The grid properties. The properties of the current slide: The name. The time position: cannot be edited for the first slide. The duration: cannot be edited (change the position of the next slide). The background color. The background image: The image allows you to choose an imported file. Edit Image allows you to apply filters and crop. Alignment determines the position of the image in the slide. Zoom determines the display size of the image.
A Representation Document allows you to display visualizations of the audio signal or imported data. The representations are superimposed in the form of layers which can be edited independently.

Above the list of representations, tap the button. The representation calculation window appears. Select a representation type. Modify the calculation parameters of the chosen representation. Tap on the Compute button. See the overview of representations to choose one suited to your musical analysis.
Select the representation to modify. Change the displayed settings.
Select the representation to delete. Use the button.

After selecting a Document, display the Property inspector with the button on the toolbar. On iPadOS, the inspector appears in the left sidebar. The Property inspector contains several tabs: The general properties of the representations: this is the first tab. The representation properties allow you to manage the visualizations displayed in the main view. The annotation layer properties.

The title of the representation as it appears in the browser. The duration: cannot be edited, it depends on the duration of the longest representation. In the background properties, the mode displays the 3 possibilities: color depending on the system interface (light or dark), choice of a specific color, choice of an imported image (import the image so that it is available in the list). local zoom allows you to locally modify the zoom of the representation. The properties of the playhead allow you to modify its display and color. Ruler and grid display horizontal (time) and vertical rulerrs; their units depend on the target chosen in the pop-up menu. Markers allows you to display and manage the display properties of time markers.

Representations displays the list of visualizations. A button opens the panel to select a new representation. A button allows you to delete the selected representation. A button in front of each representation allows you to display or hide it. A button to the right of each representation lets you drag it to change the display order. Frame opens the representation geometry management panel: Position of the representation on the vertical plane. Height of the representation on the vertical plane. Cropping of the Top of the representation. Cropping of the Bottom of the representation. Modification of Opacity. Display and change the background Color.

The first button allows you to manage the representation data. It can contain up to 4 controls: to modify the calculation of the representation. to add a data transformation: Scale modifies the size of the representation: modification of the position of the highest value. Inversion of the representation. Deformation towards the top or bottom of the representation. High pass to remove the lowest values. Low pass to remove the highest values. Modulation of the representation according to the RMS amplitude of an audio file. to modify the display of series. to display the characteristics of the representation. A button allows you to export the characteristics in Markdown format. Each representation has a specific set of properties.
A Video Document allows you to annotate a video.

After selecting a Document, display the Property inspector with the button on the toolbar. On iPadOS, the inspector appears in the left sidebar. The Property inspector contains several tabs: The general properties of the video: this is the first tab. The annotation layer properties.

The title of the video as it appears in the browser. The duration: cannot be edited, it depends on the video. The opacity of the video. The timecode display. Color adjustment: saturation, brightness and contrast. Adjustment of hue. Adding an effect. The grid properties.

You can export Documents to 4 file types: Current image. Images: only for Slideshow or Representation Documents. Video. Data. On iPadOS, exporting uses the system’s sharing and saving panels. Choose a location accessible from the Files app or share the exported file directly.
The image export formats are: JPEG HEIC PNG TIFF Quality: Low Medium High Maximum The size corresponds to the height of the image in pixels: 720p 1080p 2160p 4320p

The video export formats are: H.264 HEVC Frame rate in frames per second (FPS): 20 to 60. The size corresponds to the height of the image in pixels: 720p 1080p 2160p 4320p The bit rate corresponds to the compression rate: from 96 to 320 kb/s. Exporting Representation and Video Documents can take time. Exporting Slideshow and Canvas Documents is faster and depends on the density of annotations and their animations.
Exporting as data creates a JSON file of the Document.
A Project is iAnalyse's main working file. It contains imported files, Documents, and files created in the app, such as segmentations.
documents.s: Create and Open a Project on iPadOS

documents.t: In the iPadOS document browser, tap the create-document button. Give the Project a clear name. Save the Project in an easy-to-find location. Choose the Project strategy if iAnalyse asks you to. Import media or other files. Projects are saved as iPadOS documents. When you use iCloud Drive or another synchronization service, wait for synchronization to finish before opening the same Project on another device.

Open a Project from the iPadOS document browser or the Files app. If a linked media file cannot be found, iAnalyse may ask you to locate it again. If this happens, select the missing file's location before continuing your analysis.

iAnalyse 6 Projects are designed to be compatible with macOS and iPadOS. You can start a Project on one platform and continue it on the other. On iPadOS, the Project strategy determines how audio and video files are stored. You can prioritize a smaller Project, a Project that is easier to share between devices, or maximum quality.

iAnalyse 6 can open or import projects created with iAnalyse 5: Create a new Project. Use the iAnalyse 5 import command when it is available. Select the iAnalyse 5 project. Keep a copy of the original project before using it in iAnalyse 6. You can install different versions of iAnalyse on your computer; they can also run at the same time.
The iAnalyse interface on iPadOS is organized around a main view and a left sidebar. This sidebar contains the Project browser and the Property inspector.

The interface is organized into four areas: The toolbar contains playback, editing, and display controls. The left sidebar provides access to the Project's imported files and Documents. It also displays the Property inspector. The main view lets you view files and edit Documents. The timeline shows the current time, the media selected for playback, and every item with time-based properties.

The toolbar contains controls for the main actions: shows or hides the left sidebar. and control playback when a media file or Document is selected in the browser. The counter shows the current time and the selected media file or Document. shows the advanced playback controls. adds graphical items such as slides, markers, and filters. opens the annotation library. shows all annotations regardless of their time-based animations. shows or hides the Document timeline. shows the Property inspector in the sidebar.

The left sidebar contains the browser and the Property inspector. The browser displays all imported files, Documents, and created tools. Use it to select items to display in the main view. The inspector shows the properties of the item selected in the main view or timeline. On iPadOS, it appears in the same sidebar as the browser.
This is the workspace for graphical editing and displaying media visualizations.
The timeline shows playback progress and the time position of graphical items: annotations, markers, segmentations, and more.

iAnalyse is a workspace for audiovisual documents. It lets you bring audio, video, image, PDF, and data files together in a single Project, then create Documents to visualize, analyze, annotate, and present them.

In iAnalyse, the main file is called a Project. A Project can contain two types of items: Files, such as audio and video media, images, PDFs, MIDI, MusicXML, MEI, or data files. Documents, which are the workspaces where you analyze and organize files. A Project can contain several Documents. The available Document types are: Slideshow, for preparing a simple presentation, annotating a score, or any other use that requires multiple pages. Representation, for working with time-based or graphical visualizations of an audio signal. Video, for working with video media. Canvas, for freely arranging objects and annotations in a view. On iPadOS, each Project also has a Project strategy. It determines how iAnalyse stores audio and video files to achieve the right balance of size, quality, and portability. See Project Strategy for details.
documents.s: Understand How a Project Is Organized

documents.t: The timeline contains a visualization of the media loaded in the audiovisual player. It also lets you view and edit the time properties of items selected in the main view, as well as segmentations.

Annotations are graphical items you add to a Document to comment on, show, compare, or structure your analysis. They can contain text, graphics, or visual content. Representations display audio, MIDI, and data files in different forms: waveform, spectrogram, graph, chromagram, MFCCs, piano roll, or matrix.

The overall structure is shared by both platforms. However, two differences are important: The Project browser and Property inspector are grouped in the left sidebar. On iPadOS, drawing uses PencilKit and Apple Pencil, while macOS uses simpler mouse-based drawing. Drawings made on iPad appear as images when the Project is opened on macOS.
On iPadOS, drawn annotations use PencilKit. This integration lets you draw with Apple Pencil or your finger, depending on your system settings.

Place the playhead at the time when the drawing should appear, then choose a drawing annotation. The PencilKit palette appears, and you can draw directly in the Document. When you finish the drawing, iAnalyse saves it as a time-based annotation.

The PencilKit palette provides the drawing tools available in iPadOS: pencil, pen, eraser, color, and stroke width, depending on your system configuration. Choose a tool that remains easy to see against the Document background. For analysis, a clear drawing is more useful than a visually elaborate one.

Select the drawn annotation, then open it again with the PencilKit tools if it can be edited. You can correct strokes, erase parts, or add to the drawing. You can also change the annotation's properties in the inspector: position, size, layer, start time, and end time.
The drawing is saved in the Project with the information required to display it. When you open the Project on macOS, drawings made with PencilKit appear as images.

static/img/docs/ipados/ipados-specific/pencilkit-palette.png: the PencilKit palette open in iAnalyse. static/img/docs/ipados/ipados-specific/pencilkit-drawing-session.png: drawing in progress in a Document. static/img/docs/ipados/ipados-specific/pencilkit-selected-annotation.png: the drawn annotation selected after creation.
On iPadOS, the Project strategy determines how iAnalyse manages audio and video files on the device. It lets you balance Project size, file quality, and ease of sharing between devices.

The strategy directly affects the Project's size and how easily you can share it. Choose a strategy when you create or prepare the Project, then check it before transferring the Project to another device. You can change this strategy at any time in the Project's advanced menu. If the Project contains linked videos and you switch to a more self-contained strategy, iAnalyse may offer to embed those videos in the Project.

This strategy is recommended for music-analysis projects, listening guides, teaching materials, and Projects that mainly use images. It reduces the amount of storage used. Audio is imported into the Project and converted to M4A. Video remains linked to the source file. The Project uses less storage.

This strategy is suitable when you want to open your Projects easily on multiple iOS, iPadOS, or macOS devices. Audio is imported into the Project and converted to M4A. Video is copied into the Project. The Project is more self-contained and portable. Copied videos can use a significant amount of storage.

This strategy is suitable for advanced use and signal analysis when you want to preserve audio files in their original format. Audio is copied without conversion. Video is copied into the Project. Audio quality is preserved. This strategy uses more storage.
Use Save Space to reduce Project size, Cross-Device Sharing to move Projects between devices, and Maximum Quality when preserving the original files is the priority.

static/img/docs/ipados/ipados-specific/project-strategy-choice.png: the strategy selection screen. static/img/docs/ipados/ipados-specific/project-strategy-current.png: a Project showing the active strategy. static/img/docs/ipados/ipados-specific/project-strategy-options.png: details of the three strategies.

Markers are used to identify temporal positions. They allow you to quickly find an event, the start of a section, a transition or a point to comment on. You cannot add markers directly to files; you must create a Document to use markers.

Place the playhead at the desired position, then tap the button on the toolbar and choose Add Marker. The marker is created and appears in the timeline. If the open Document is a representation, the marker also appears in the main view.
Select the marker and open the inspector with the button on the toolbar to view its properties in the left sidebar. You can modify its title, position or color.
You can change how markers appear in the timeline in its properties. You can change how markers appear in the main view of a Representation Document in its properties.
Select the marker and use Delete in the editing actions.

Markers are particularly useful in long Projects. Use them as reference points to quickly return to a section, compare multiple moments, or prepare a presentation. See the Touch gestures page for details.

You can import markers from other software when they are available in a text file (.txt or .csv). The file must contain a first time column (in seconds or milliseconds), then a column for the label. Example structure: 0.000000 Label 1 0.011610 Label 2 0.023220 Label 3 0.034830 Label 4 You cannot import markers into a digital audio file: markers can only be imported into Documents. To import markers contained in a text file: Open a Document. Choose Import > Markers.

A segmentation is used to: Represent key moments. Represent the return of a theme or an instrument in music, of a character or a framing in a film, of a position in a performance, etc. Represent the different parts of a structure. Represent the musical form on several levels. You cannot add segmentation to a digital audio file; segmentations are only added to Documents.

The segmentation is displayed in the timeline of a Document. To view and edit it, tap the button on the timeline. All five layers are displayed by default. When you create a Project, it contains a segmentation by default. This segmentation can be displayed in all Project Documents. You can modify it or create new ones. The segmentations are at the project level and not at the Document level. This allows you to display the same segmentation in multiple Documents. You can create as many segmentations as you want.
A segmentation contains segments that are associated with a layer.
To create a segment, simply double-tap in the target layer. By default, created segments only have a start time and last until the next segment or the end of the media.
Select the segment and use Delete in the editing actions.

To move the start time of a segment, touch its start, then drag the selection area that appears. To edit the other properties of a segment: Select the segment. Show the inspector with the timeline button . On iPadOS, it appears in the left sidebar. In the inspector, select the tab. Segments have the following properties: There are 3 Types of segments: : segment which only represents an instant; it appears in the form of a rectangle with a transparency gradient. : segment which continues until the next one or until the end if there is none. : segment which has a specific start and end. The segments are associated with one of the Layers of the segmentation. Segments have a Label in the form of text or a symbol to choose from the list. The segments have a Color. Segments have a Start time. It has several properties: The Type can take two states: for a sharp start. for a gradual start, represented by a transparency gradient. The temporal Position. The gradient Interval when using a type. Segments of type have an End time. It has several properties: The Type can take two states: for a sharp end. for a gradual end, represented by a transparency gradient. The end temporal Position. The gradient Interval when using a type.
To edit the segmentation properties: Show the inspector with the timeline button . On iPadOS, it appears in the left sidebar. In the inspector, select the tab.

The first section of the Segmentations Property inspector allows you to: Hide or show segmentation. Modify the segmentation. The button allows you to display the segmentations available in the Project: Double-tap on the segmentation name to modify it. Select to add segmentation. Select to delete a segmentation. Select to duplicate a segmentation.

You can disable snapping between segments. Type allows you to display a segmentation in several forms: A Linear representation is the default display. Segments from all layers are shown. A Formal Diagram represents the segments of a layer by classifying them according to their label (text or symbol) and by order of appearance. An Arc diagram allows you to visualize the patterns that repeat in the segments of a layer. A Distance Matrix compares each segment with all other segments of the layer. A red box appears when the two segments have the same identity (same title or same symbol). The two axes represent time. The diagonal corresponds to each segment compared to itself and can be hidden with the Hide Identity option. A Sequence Matrix searches for identical consecutive sequences. Each line corresponds to a repeated pattern and the rectangles indicate its different occurrences on the time axis. The pattern size parameter sets the number of consecutive segments to compare, with a minimum of two. A State-transition diagram allows you to visualize the sequences of patterns according to the property Pattern min. Concerning matrices, for example, with the segmentation A – B – C – A – B – D: The distance matrix connects the two A's and the two B's separately. The sequence matrix detects the repetition of pattern A – B if the Pattern min. is 2.

There are 3 properties: Color modes: : no color is displayed. : the complete line is colored. : a small color strip is drawn at the start of the line. Show horizontal Lines separating layers. Show Labels at the start of the line.

Show Labels of segments. Change the Size of the labels. Color modes: The color of the Segment. Same: same color. Color of the Layer. Alternate between 2 colors. Depending on the Label of the segment. Depending on the Duration of the segment. Opacity of the segments.
Importing adds files to the Project so that they can be played, annotated, represented or used in a Document.

Importing audio and video files follows the same procedure: Use the Import > Audio or Video menu. Select one or more files, then confirm their addition to the Project. A preview of the file appears in the main view. If you open the Property inspector, it displays all the file’s properties. The supported formats are: Audio: WAV, AIFF, MP3, M4A, FLAC. Video: MP4, M4V, MOV. In preferences, on the Advanced tab, you can select how the audio files are imported: Automatic (default): uncompressed files are imported without modification. Compressed files are converted to AAC at 320 Kbps. Force Compression (AAC): all audio files are compressed to AAC at 320 Kbps when imported. On iPadOS, the Project strategy also affects audio and video imports. See Project strategy.
documents.s: Import an audio or video file

documents.t: Images can be used as visual sources, surfaces for annotations or elements integrated into a Document. To import an image: Use the Import > Image menu. Select one or more files, then confirm their addition to the Project. A preview of the file appears in the main view. If you open the Property inspector, it displays all the file’s properties. The supported formats are: JPG, JPEG, BMP, PNG, TIF, TIFF, HEIF and HEIC. Images are automatically converted to HEIC format.

PDFs are imported as images. To import a PDF: Use the Import > PDF menu. Select one or more files, then confirm their addition to the Project. A PDF appears as a group of images in the browser. Each image can be displayed in the main view. If you open the Property inspector, it displays all the file’s properties. The PDF pages are saved in HEIC format.

iAnalyse can import MIDI, MusicXML and MEI files. These files are transformed into a format that can be used as media for creating a Document. The audiovisual player uses the internal synthesizer in macOS or iPadOS to play the file. To import a music file: Use the Import menu and choose MIDI, MusicXML or MEI. Select one or more files, then confirm their addition to the Project. Each file can be displayed in the main view. If you open the Property inspector, it displays all the file’s properties. The supported formats are: MID, MIDI, MusicXML, MXL, MEI

Data files allow you to add time-based values calculated or produced by other software to the Project. This data can then be displayed in graphical representations or used in certain calculations. The supported formats are: TXT, CSV

A data file generally contains a first column of time, then one or more columns of values. Example structure: 0.000000 0.00 0.011610 2.54 0.023220 6.84 0.034830 0.00 The first column indicates the time position. The following columns contain the values to represent.

Before confirming the import, check the data preview. Check in particular: The column separator. The time unit. The minimum and maximum values. The name assigned to the imported data. The number of series detected. An inconsistent preview often indicates a bad separator, incorrect time unit, or poorly formatted file.

You can import a segmentation when the temporal structure has been prepared in another tool. After importing, check the segment start times, end times and names in the timeline. An imported segmentation can then be modified like a segmentation created directly in iAnalyse. A segmentation file contains a first time column, then a column with segment labels. Example structure: 0.000000 Partie 1 10.011610 Partie 2 26 Partie 3 45.05 Partie 4 The structure of the data in the file must follow the example above. The supported formats are: TXT, CSV
Scala files allow you to add information related to scales or pitches. After import, check that the values correspond to the musical context of the Project. The supported format is: SCL
Once imported, the data can be selected in compatible representations: graph, gradient, fundamental frequency, matrix, chromagram or MFCCs depending on the file type.
Imported files are the sources used by the Documents and representations in the Project.

The browser displays the files available in the Project. Select a file to view its data and information. A single Project can contain several types of files: audio, video, image, PDF, MIDI, MusicXML, MEI, data, etc.
A file can only be deleted if it is no longer used in the Project. In the browser, swipe left on the file’s row, then tap Delete File.

Depending on the selected strategy, some video files may remain linked to their source files. In this case, iAnalyse may offer to locate them or copy them into the Project. If you are preparing a Project to share with macOS or another iPad, check the Project strategy before transferring it.
Playback controls allow you to listen to or watch the active media while following the position in the timeline and Document.

Use the playback command in the toolbar to start or stop the active media. The playhead moves in the timeline and the Document's time elements update based on the current position. You can return to the beginning of the media or move directly to another position from the timeline: Use the Stop button to stop playback and return to the beginning. Touch the playhead: a wider selection strip appears. Drag it to move the playhead. Use the available playback controls to move through the media. See Gestures and controls for available interactions.
The counter displays the time position of the playhead from the beginning. It also indicates the media used. Tap the counter to access the playback settings.

The playback settings allow you to modify: The volume (speaker symbol). Playback speed without changing the pitch (metronome symbol). The transposition of the pitch (tuning fork symbol) without changing the speed. By default, the transposition is by semitone, but it is possible to uncheck this option to do a continuous transposition. The inversion of the counter counting down the remaining time. The display of a countdown before the start of playback. You can display this view permanently by touching on the area at the top above the text and then dragging it to detach it.

In the timeline, it is possible to select a playback range by touching and dragging on the timeline ruler. This range is then played in a loop and the symbol appears next to the counter in the toolbar: Touch and drag on the time ruler to draw the area to loop. Touch and release to cancel loop playback.
The timeline displays the temporal organization of the Project. It is used to monitor playback, navigate media, move annotations, display markers and work with segmentations.

The timeline is read from left to right. The current position is indicated by the playhead. A graduated ruler indicates time positions in minutes:seconds. Annotations, markers, segmentations, and temporal representations are displayed in the timeline. You can show or hide the timeline with the toolbar button ().

Tap the time ruler to place the playhead at a specific position. You can also drag it to browse the media. When playback is active, the playhead advances automatically. Items synced with time update in the main view.

The zoom slider at the bottom left allows you to work at different scales: Zoom out to see the entire Project. Zoom in to precisely adjust an annotation, a marker or the segment of a segmentation. To the right of the zoom slider, you find different controls: : cancels zoom to view the entire timeline. : activates playhead tracking; it always remains visible while the media is playing. : activates timeline scrolling; the playhead always remains in the center. : for Video Documents, divides the timeline into two parts. : displays the segmentation in the timeline. : opens the timeline display options. This panel provides access to the most common options. To view all options, use the Property inspector. : Opens the timeline Property inspector.

The timeline allows you to select time elements. Once an element is selected, you can adjust its position, duration or properties from the inspector. But you can also adjust these temporal properties in the timeline. For example, for annotations: Select the annotation in the main view. In the timeline, the annotation occupies the entire height. Touch the beginning, end or middle of the annotation. A colored band appears; drag it to adjust the annotation. If the selection strips do not appear or are not active, increase the zoom slider a little.
documents.s: Select and edit the temporal properties of an element

documents.t: Preferences define the general behavior of iAnalyse on iPadOS. They allow you to adapt the application to your way of working without modifying the content of a particular Project. General preferences. Document preferences. Annotation preferences. Audio import preferences. Advanced preferences. The Project strategy is configured separately within the Project itself. See Project strategy.
On iPadOS, use toolbar controls, action menus and touch gestures. Not all macOS shortcuts are available on iPad.

Gesture Function Tap an annotation Select the annotation Drag an annotation or a handle Change its position or size Double-tap a polygon, Bézier shape or cursor Edit its points or keyframes Double-tap while creating a shape Finish creating the shape Touch and hold a keyframe Open its context menu to delete it Double-tap in a segmentation layer Add a segment Drag on the time ruler Define a playback loop Tap and release on the time ruler Cancel the loop Swipe left on a file row in the browser Show the delete command Available gestures depend on the selected item and editing mode. Drawing uses PencilKit and Apple Pencil.
Double-tap a time field to enter a value in 00:00.000 format (minutes:seconds:milliseconds). See Edit annotations.

When the floating video window receives keyboard input, these shortcuts are available: Shortcut Function Space Play / pause Return Stop Escape Close the floating video window These shortcuts apply to this window; use the playback buttons in other views.
This page brings together the most common problems and the first steps to try before making major changes to a Project.

If iAnalyse can no longer find media, check that the file has not been moved, renamed, or deleted. Use the location command provided to indicate its new location. If the Project must be shared, choose a strategy or format that copies the necessary media into the Project.
A Project can become large when it contains videos, copied media, high definition images or numerous calculations. Delete unused files where possible. Also check the Project strategy.

If a file doesn't import, check its format, extension, and contents. For data files, check the column separator, time unit, and value structure. Try importing a simple file to check if the problem is with the format or the file itself.

If an export fails, try a smaller size or more compatible format first. High-resolution video exports can take a long time and take up a lot of disk space. Also check that the Project is saved and that the export location is accessible. You can also export to the iPad’s local storage, rather than an external drive or cloud storage.

Always keep a copy of the original Project before opening it in iAnalyse 6. After import, check the media, annotations, representations and segmentations. Imported Slideshow Documents may look different. This is expected; allow time to adjust them.
To improve responsiveness, reduce the elements displayed simultaneously, hide unnecessary layers, close unnecessary views, and avoid heavy representations during editing.

If the application suddenly closes when opening a Project located in the cloud, verify that the synchronization is complete. This issue can occur when you open a Project that has just been edited on another device, or when you reopen a Project on the same device without waiting for syncing to complete. Avoid opening the same file on macOS and iPadOS at the same time.
documents.s: Problem with using files in the cloud

documents.t: The annotation library allows you to save annotations or groups of annotations for reuse in other Documents or other Projects.

Open the library from the toolbar with the button. You can select: Recently used annotations. The User annotations that you imported into the library. Media: images or videos imported into the Project that you can use as annotations. The different categories of annotations.

Annotations added to the library are available for all projects. Select an annotation in the main view of a Document. Choose Edit > Add Annotation to User Library. The annotation is added to the User category of the library. You can delete an annotation added to the library: Click on the icon at the top right of the annotation.
documents.s: Add an annotation to the library

documents.t: Annotations are graphics, text, images or videos that you can add to Documents. You cannot add annotations directly to files; you must create a Document to use the annotations.

First place the playhead at the time position where the annotation should appear. Open the annotation library with the button on the toolbar. Select a category and an annotation. The annotation appears in the main view. In a Representation Document, if the playhead is outside the visible area of the main view, the annotation is added at the center of the view.

When you add a line, polygon or Bézier curve annotation, no annotation is added immediately to the main view: Click to add points: at least 2 for lines and 3 for polygons and Bézier curves. Double-click on the final point. The annotation then appears in the main view.

When you add a drawing annotation, no annotation is added immediately to the main view: Just draw in the main view. When you release the mouse button, the annotation is added. On iPadOS, drawing uses PencilKit which is not available on macOS. Drawings added on iPadOS therefore appear as images when the Project is opened on macOS.

Cursors are somewhat special annotations: they appear in the form of animated graphics based on keyframes. They are used to create playheads that move on a score to the rhythm of the music or annotations that highlight the sequence of several notes or chords. Cursors can only be created in Slideshow Documents. There are four types of cursors: : horizontal scrolling. : vertical scrolling. : circular scrolling. : scrolling following a line. You can add multiple cursors to each slide. There are two techniques for adding cursors: Manual: you adjust each keyframe manually. This is ideal for creating a playhead on a slightly complex score or one that has tempo variations. Easy: you adjust the time synchronization during playback. This technique is ideal for scores at a moderate tempo in which there are no or few tempo variations.

Position the playhead at the moment where the cursor should appear. Click the button on the toolbar and choose Add Manual Cursor. In the window that opens, choose the cursor properties: Its Type. Its Shape. Not all shapes are available for all types. The number of Keyframes: you can add or delete keyframes later. This number includes the first and last keyframes at the ends of the cursor. Whether the position of the shape should be Interpolated between keyframes. The Color. Click Add. You cannot change the Type of a cursor once it is added. With the exception of Type, all of these properties can then be edited with the Property inspector.

Position the playhead at the moment where the cursor should appear. Click the button on the toolbar and choose Add Easy Cursor. The right panel opens and allows you to manage the steps: Step 1: mark the graphical positions. By moving the cursor on the main view, you can click to position the keyframes, for example on the beats of the score inserted as the slide background. You can change the cursor's Size and Color in the right panel. Step 2: Click Time-based positions in the right panel. Start playback and click on the main view to associate a time position with each graphic position. Step 3: Click Finalize in the right panel. The cursor is created on the main view.

Select the cursor and open the inspector with the toolbar button to display its properties. Specific cursor properties can be found in the tab: Modify the Shape. Not all shapes are available for all types. Change the Direction of the triangular shape. Enable or disable Interpolation between keyframes. Keyframe Animation: apply annotation animation to each keyframe. Smoothing: smoothes the line for type cursors. Width of certain cursor types. Size of certain cursor types. Center size of type cursors. Path: only for types : Visible: display the line followed by the cursor. Hide shape. Size of the shape. Selected Frame: this is the keyframe currently displayed in the main view: Last Frame: display the properties of the last keyframe. Interpolation: interpolate with the next keyframe. Position between 0.0 and 1.0. Time. Color. Opacity.
Select the cursor and press the key, or choose Edit > Delete.

To change a cursor's keyframes: Double-click it; the cursor switches to advanced editing mode. You can change the position of a keyframe in the main view by clicking and dragging the corresponding handle You can add a keyframe by positioning the cursor between 2 keyframes, a handle appears on which you can click. You can delete a keyframe by holding down the Control key, the keyframe handle changes to and you can click to delete it In the timeline, keyframes appear as vertical lines: Move the pointer near a keyframe to reveal its selection area. Click and drag. You cannot delete or add keyframes in the timeline; you must do it in the main view.
You can edit the properties of an annotation in several ways.

Click the annotation and change its position or size using the selection handles. If the annotation is a line, you can move it using its handles at both ends. If the annotation is a polygon or Bézier curve, double-click to edit the points: Click and drag the point handles. Position the cursor between two points and click to add a new point. Hold down the Control key and move the pointer near a point. The handle changes to ; click it to remove the point. You can also select multiple annotations to move or resize them together: Click outside of annotations and drag to select multiple annotations. Or use the key and click on the annotations to select. Edit the bounding box that contains the selected annotations.

When an annotation is selected in the main view, a rectangle appears in the timeline: Move the cursor to the start, center or end. Draggable areas appear in the accent color. Click and drag to change temporal properties.
Open the inspector with the button on the toolbar to modify all the properties.
Open the inspector with the toolbar button, then use the tab to edit the annotation animations. You can add entry, exit, and content animations.
Select the annotation and press the key, or choose Edit > Delete.

Layers allow you to organize the annotations of a Document. They are useful for separating multiple levels of analysis, displaying only certain annotations, or controlling their behavior during playback.

Each annotation belongs to a layer. A Project can use as many layers as you want. For example, you can use one layer for general comments, another for musical elements, and another for visual cues, etc.

To display the layer editing interface, use the last tab of the Document properties. You can also edit a layer from an annotation with the button located to the right of the drop-down menu allowing you to choose the layer.
Select a layer from the top list. Use the button to add a layer. Use the button to delete a layer.

In the layers list, you can: Use the button to hide or show the layer annotations. Use the button to lock the layer annotations. In this case, you can no longer edit their graphic or temporal position in the main view and the timeline, but the inspector properties remain available. You can also use the controls below the list: Modify the Title of the layer. Visible: show or hide the layer annotations. Locked: lock the graphic and temporal editing of layer annotations.
documents.s: Show, hide or lock a layer

documents.t: Layers can control how annotations appear during playback. Depending on the settings, annotations can follow their temporal duration, maintain a common color or opacity, or take on a different appearance outside of their active duration. Select a layer from the list: the properties are displayed below. Time Animation: track the start and end temporal properties of annotations to determine their display. Mode: Start and Stay: Once the layer annotations appear, they remain displayed. Continuous: the layer's annotations always remain displayed, and you can modify their color and opacity outside their time range with the two properties below. Color: color annotations outside their time range. Opacity: change the opacity of annotations outside their time range. Layers in Representation Documents default to Mode > Continuous.

With iAnalyse, you work from imported files by creating Documents. There are 4 types of Documents: Slideshow, to prepare a simple presentation, annotate a score or any other use in which you need several pages. Representation, to work with temporal or graphic visualizations. Video, to work with video media. Canvas, to freely organize objects and annotations on a view.

To create a Document, first select an audiovisual or music file (MIDI, MusicXML, or MEI). Choose File > New, then choose one of the Document types at the top of the list. Video Documents can only be created from a file with a video track.

Documents include 2 elements: The editing view, which occupies the largest area: it is the view which will be exported, for example as an image or video. The timeline under the editing view: it displays the temporal properties of the elements selected in the editing view.
The grid appears on the editing view. Depending on the Documents, it can take several forms.

The regular grid is present in Slideshow, Video and Canvas Documents. It is managed by 5 properties: Visibility. Magnetism for annotations. Mode: grid or points. The spacing determines the size of the grid. Divisions determines the number of subdivisions of the grid.

In the representations, the grid and the vertical rulerr are combined and the properties are distributed over two panels. The representation properties inspector provides access to general properties: Display allows you to display the time ruler, vertical rulerr and grid. Target determines the representation that will be used to construct the vertical rulerr and the grid. Mode determines the vertical ruler to use for musical representations (logarithmic spectrogram, fundamental frequency, etc.): frequencies or musical pitches. To display the vertical rulerr and horizontal grid lines, you must select a representation in the Target property. The advanced properties panel is displayed by clicking the button. Advanced properties: grid: Set the display of the vertical and horizontal lines of the grid. Color of the grid. Opacity of the grid. Mode determines the ruler to use for musical representations (logarithmic spectrogram, fundamental frequency, etc.): frequencies or musical pitches. Advanced properties: pitch graduations: These controls are only active if a musical representation is selected in Target and Pitch is selected in Mode. A3 Frequency: the reference tuning frequency. Element: the line of the note to edit. Visibility [grid and ruler]: display of the note. Octave [ruler]: display of the octave number. Min. Range and Max. Range [grid and ruler]: allow you to reduce the displayed pitch range. Color [grid and ruler]. Line [grid]: thicker or dotted line. Pitch parameters are only active with representations based on logarithmic frequency visualization or musical pitch extraction.
A Canvas Document displays a resizable graphic space on which you can add annotations.

After selecting a Document, display the Property inspector with the button on the toolbar. The Property inspector contains several tabs: The general properties of the canvas: this is the first tab. The annotation layer properties.

The title of the canvas as it appears in the browser. The width of the canvas. The height of the canvas. In the background properties, the mode displays the 3 possibilities: color depending on the system interface (light or dark), choice of a specific color, choice of an imported image (import the image so that it is available in the list). The grid properties.
A Slideshow Document consists of slides in which you can insert a background image and annotations.
Position the playhead in the timeline where you want to add the slide. Select the button from the toolbar. Click Add Slide.

Open the Property inspector by clicking the button on the toolbar. Edit the properties of the Slide. You can also edit the time position of the slide in the timeline: Move the pointer to the start of the slide. The selection bar appears in color. Click and drag. The Slide part of the inspector displays the properties of the slide displayed in the main view. Use the Timeline playhead to change the displayed slide.
Show the slide to be deleted in the main view. Choose Edit > Delete. The first slide cannot be deleted.

After selecting a Document, display the Property inspector with the button on the toolbar. The Property inspector contains several tabs: The general properties of the slideshow: this is the first tab. The annotation layer properties.

The title of the slideshow as it appears in the browser. The ratio determines the size of the slideshow slides. The grid properties. The properties of the current slide: The name. The time position: cannot be edited for the first slide. The duration: cannot be edited (change the position of the next slide). The background color. The background image: The image allows you to choose an imported file. Edit Image allows you to apply filters and crop. Alignment determines the position of the image in the slide. Zoom determines the display size of the image.
A Representation Document allows you to display visualizations of the audio signal or imported data. The representations are superimposed in the form of layers which can be edited independently.

Above the list of representations, click the button. The representation calculation window appears. Select a representation type. Modify the calculation parameters of the chosen representation. Click on the Compute button. See the overview of representations to choose one suited to your musical analysis.
Select the representation to modify. Change the displayed settings.
Select the representation to delete. Use the button.

After selecting a Document, display the Property inspector with the button on the toolbar. The Property inspector contains several tabs: The general properties of the representations: this is the first tab. The representation properties allow you to manage the visualizations displayed in the main view. The annotation layer properties.

The title of the representation as it appears in the browser. The duration: cannot be edited, it depends on the duration of the longest representation. In the background properties, the mode displays the 3 possibilities: color depending on the system interface (light or dark), choice of a specific color, choice of an imported image (import the image so that it is available in the list). local zoom allows you to locally modify the zoom of the representation. The properties of the playhead allow you to modify its display and color. Ruler and grid display horizontal (time) and vertical rulerrs; their units depend on the target chosen in the pop-up menu. Markers allows you to display and manage the display properties of time markers.

Representations displays the list of visualizations. A button opens the window to select a new representation. A button allows you to delete the selected representation. A button in front of each representation allows you to display or hide it. A button to the right of each representation allows you to move it to modify the display order. Frame opens the representation geometry management panel: Position of the representation on the vertical plane. Height of the representation on the vertical plane. Cropping of the Top of the representation. Cropping of the Bottom of the representation. Modification of Opacity. Display and change the background Color.

The first button allows you to manage the representation data. It can contain up to 4 controls: to modify the calculation of the representation. to add a data transformation: Scale modifies the size of the representation: modification of the position of the highest value. Inversion of the representation. Deformation towards the top or bottom of the representation. High pass to remove the lowest values. Low pass to remove the highest values. Modulation of the representation according to the RMS amplitude of an audio file. to modify the display of series. to display the characteristics of the representation. A button allows you to export the characteristics in Markdown format. Each representation has a specific set of properties.
A Video Document allows you to annotate a video.

After selecting a Document, display the Property inspector with the button on the toolbar. The Property inspector contains several tabs: The general properties of the video: this is the first tab. The annotation layer properties.

The title of the video as it appears in the browser. The duration: cannot be edited, it depends on the video. The opacity of the video. The timecode display. Color adjustment: saturation, brightness and contrast. Adjustment of hue. Adding an effect. The grid properties.
You can export Documents to 4 file types: Current image. Images: only for Slideshow or Representation Documents. Video. Data.
The image export formats are: JPEG HEIC PNG TIFF Quality: Low Medium High Maximum The size corresponds to the height of the image in pixels: 720p 1080p 2160p 4320p

The video export formats are: H.264 HEVC Frame rate in frames per second (FPS): 20 to 60. The size corresponds to the height of the image in pixels: 720p 1080p 2160p 4320p The bit rate corresponds to the compression rate: from 96 to 320 kb/s. Exporting Representation and Video Documents can take time. Exporting Slideshow and Canvas Documents is faster and depends on the density of the annotations and their animations.
Exporting as data creates a JSON file of the Document.
A Project is the main working file of iAnalyse. It contains imported files, Documents and files created in the application, such as segmentations.

Create a new Project using the File > New > Project menu. Give the Project a clear name. Save the Project in an easy-to-find location. Import media or files. It is recommended to save the Project regularly with the File > Save… menu or the shortcut ⌘S.

Open a Project using the File > Open… or File > Open Recent menu. If linked media cannot be found, iAnalyse may ask you to locate it again. In this case, specify the location of the missing file before continuing the analysis.

iAnalyse 6 Projects are designed to be compatible between macOS and iPadOS. You can therefore start a Project on one platform and continue it on the other. On macOS, Projects are saved in the most complete and compatible format. This format may take up more disk space, but it simplifies exchanges between devices.

iAnalyse 6 can open or import projects created with iAnalyse 5: Create a new Project. Use the File > Import > iAnalyse 5 menu. Select the iAnalyse 5 project. Keep a copy of the original project before using it in iAnalyse 6. You can install the different versions of iAnalyse on your computer; they can also run at the same time.
Some editing parameters are present in several places in the interface.

Many parameters use sliders to edit values. If you want to edit the value precisely: Use CTRL + click on the slider. A popover view opens containing several controls. Enter the value and select the Apply button.
When you modify the temporal properties of an object, you have 3 possibilities: Editing by units with the keyboard. Editing by units with the pointer. Manual editing.

Click on one of the units (minutes:seconds:milliseconds). The unit is selected. Use the and keys to change the unit value in increments of +/-1. Hold down the key and use the and keys to change the unit value in intervals of +/- 10 for minutes/seconds and +/- 100 for milliseconds.
documents.s: Editing by units with the keyboard

documents.t: Click on one of the units (minutes:seconds:milliseconds). The unit is selected. Click and drag up or down to cycle through values by +/-1. Hold down the key and click-drag up or down to scroll the values in intervals of +/- 10 for minutes/seconds and +/- 100 for milliseconds.
documents.s: Editing by units with the pointer

documents.t: Double-click to enter the time value using the syntax: 00:00.000 (minutes:seconds:milliseconds). The syntax must be exact (number of digits, position of : and .) for the value to be taken into account.
The properties panels feature two types of buttons to access advanced functions.
The symbol is used in buttons that allow access to specific actions through a menu.
The symbol is used in buttons that open popover views with advanced functions.

The font selection for text editing offers two options: Multi allows you to use only fonts available on both platforms (macOS and iPadOS). Computer allows you to use all fonts available on macOS. If the font is not available when the project is opened on iPadOS, it will be replaced with Helvetica.
The iAnalyse interface is organized around a single window allowing you to navigate between imported files and created Documents.

The interface is organized into 5 parts: The toolbar groups together playback, editing and display commands. The browser provides access to imported files and Project Documents. The main view allows you to view files and modify Documents. The timeline displays the time position, the media selected for playback, and any elements with time properties. The Property inspector displays the settings for the selected item.

The toolbar includes commands for the main actions: shows or hides the browser. and control playback when a media file or Document is selected in the browser. The counter displays the time position and the media file activated for playback. shows advanced playback controls. allows you to add graphic elements like slides, markers, filters, etc. opens the annotation library. displays all annotations independently of their temporal animations. shows or hides the Documents timeline. shows or hides the Property inspector.
The browser displays all imported files, Documents and tools created. It allows you to select the elements to display in the main view.
This is the space for graphical editing and display of multimedia visualizations.
The timeline displays the playback progress and the temporal position of the graphic elements: annotations, markers, segmentations, etc.
The inspector displays the properties of the selected item in the main view or timeline.

iAnalyse is a workspace for audiovisual documents. It allows you to bring together audio, video, image, PDF or data files in the same Project, then create Documents to view, analyze, annotate and present them.

In iAnalyse, the main file is called a Project. A Project can contain two types of elements: Files, such as audio or video media, images, PDFs, MIDI files, MusicXML, MEI or data files. Documents, which are the workspaces in which you analyze and organize files. A Project can contain several Documents. The types of Documents available are: Slideshow, to prepare a simple presentation, annotate a score or any other use in which you need several pages. Representation, to work with temporal or graphic visualizations of the audio signal. Video, to work on video media. Canvas, to freely organize objects and annotations on a view.
documents.s: Understand the organization of a Project

documents.t: The timeline contains the visualization of the media loaded in the audiovisual player. It also allows you to view and modify the temporal properties of the elements selected in the main view as well as the segmentations.

Annotations are the graphic elements that you add to the Document to comment, show, compare or structure the analysis. They can be textual, graphic or visual. The representations allow you to display audio, MIDI files and data in different forms: waveform, spectrogram, graph, chromagram, MFCCs, piano roll or matrix.

The general structure is common to both platforms. However, two differences are important: On iPadOS, you can choose a Project strategy to control file size and Project portability. Indeed, tablets do not always have as much storage as a computer. On iPadOS, drawing uses PencilKit and Apple Pencil, while macOS uses simpler mouse drawing. Drawings made on the iPad appear as images when the Project is open on macOS.

Markers are used to identify temporal positions. They allow you to quickly find an event, the start of a section, a transition or a point to comment on. You cannot add markers directly to files; you must create a Document to use markers.

Place the playhead at the desired position, then click the button on the toolbar and choose Add Marker. The marker is created and appears in the timeline. If the open Document is a representation, the marker also appears in the main view.
Select the marker and open the inspector with the button on the toolbar to view its properties. You can modify its title, position or color.
You can change how markers appear in the timeline in its properties. You can change how markers appear in the main view of a Representation Document in its properties.
Select the marker and press the key, or choose Edit > Delete.

Markers are particularly useful in long Projects. Use them as reference points to quickly return to a section, compare multiple moments, or prepare a presentation. See the Keyboard shortcuts and gestures page for details.

You can import markers from other software when they are available in a text file (.txt or .csv). The file must contain a first time column (in seconds or milliseconds), then a column for the label. Example structure: 0.000000 Label 1 0.011610 Label 2 0.023220 Label 3 0.034830 Label 4 You cannot import markers into a digital audio file: markers can only be imported into Documents. To import markers contained in a text file: Open a Document. Choose File > Import > Markers.

A segmentation is used to: Represent key moments. Represent the return of a theme or an instrument in music, of a character or a framing in a film, of a position in a performance, etc. Represent the different parts of a structure. Represent the musical form on several levels. You cannot add segmentation to a digital audio file; segmentations are only added to Documents.

The segmentation is displayed in the timeline of a Document. To view and edit it, click the button on the timeline. All five layers are displayed by default. When you create a Project, it contains a segmentation by default. This segmentation can be displayed in all Project Documents. You can modify it or create new ones. The segmentations are at the project level and not at the Document level. This allows you to display the same segmentation in multiple Documents. You can create as many segmentations as you want.
A segmentation contains segments that are associated with a layer.
To create a segment, simply double-click in the target layer. By default, created segments only have a start time and last until the next segment or the end of the media.
Select the segment and press the key, or choose Edit > Delete.

To move the start time of a segment, move the cursor near its start, then click and drag on the selection box that appears. To edit the other properties of a segment: Select the segment. Show the inspector with the timeline button . In the inspector, select the tab. Segments have the following properties: There are 3 Types of segments: : segment which only represents an instant; it appears in the form of a rectangle with a transparency gradient. : segment which continues until the next one or until the end if there is none. : segment which has a specific start and end. The segments are associated with one of the Layers of the segmentation. Segments have a Label in the form of text or a symbol to choose from the list. The segments have a Color. Segments have a Start time. It has several properties: The Type can take two states: for a sharp start. for a gradual start, represented by a transparency gradient. The temporal Position. The gradient Interval when using a type. Segments of type have an End time. It has several properties: The Type can take two states: for a sharp end. for a gradual end, represented by a transparency gradient. The end temporal Position. The gradient Interval when using a type.
To edit the segmentation properties: Show the inspector with the timeline button . In the inspector, select the tab.

The first section of the Segmentations Property inspector allows you to: Hide or show segmentation. Modify the segmentation. The button allows you to display the segmentations available in the Project: Double-click on the segmentation name to modify it. Select to add segmentation. Select to delete a segmentation. Select to duplicate a segmentation.

You can disable snapping between segments. Type allows you to display a segmentation in several forms: A Linear representation is the default display. Segments from all layers are shown. A Formal Diagram represents the segments of a layer by classifying them according to their label (text or symbol) and by order of appearance. An Arc diagram allows you to visualize the patterns that repeat in the segments of a layer. A Distance Matrix compares each segment with all other segments of the layer. A red box appears when the two segments have the same identity (same title or same symbol). The two axes represent time. The diagonal corresponds to each segment compared to itself and can be hidden with the Hide Identity option. A Sequence Matrix searches for identical consecutive sequences. Each line corresponds to a repeated pattern and the rectangles indicate its different occurrences on the time axis. The pattern size parameter sets the number of consecutive segments to compare, with a minimum of two. A State-transition diagram allows you to visualize the sequences of patterns according to the property Pattern min. Concerning matrices, for example, with the segmentation A – B – C – A – B – D: The distance matrix connects the two A's and the two B's separately. The sequence matrix detects the repetition of pattern A – B if the Pattern min. is 2.

Importing adds files to the Project so that they can be played, annotated, represented or used in a Document.

Importing audio and video files follows the same procedure: Use the File > Import > Audio or Video menu. Select one or more files, then confirm their addition to the Project. A preview of the file appears in the main view. If you open the Property inspector, it displays all the file’s properties. The supported formats are: Audio: WAV, AIFF, MP3, M4A, FLAC. Video: MP4, M4V, MOV. In the preferences (iAnalyse > Preferences… menu, then the Advanced tab), you can select how the audio files are imported: Automatic (default): uncompressed files are imported without modification. Compressed files are converted to AAC at 320 Kbps. Force Compression (AAC): all audio files are compressed to AAC at 320 Kbps when imported.
