documents.t: Images can be used as visual sources, surfaces for annotations or elements integrated into a Document. To import an image: Use the File > Import > Image menu. Select one or more files, then confirm their addition to the Project. A preview of the file appears in the main view. If you open the Property inspector, it displays all the file’s properties. The supported formats are: JPG, JPEG, BMP, PNG, TIF, TIFF, HEIF and HEIC. Images are automatically converted to HEIC format.

PDFs are imported as images. To import a PDF: Use the File > Import > PDF menu. Select one or more files, then confirm their addition to the Project. A PDF appears as a group of images in the browser. Each image can be displayed in the main view. If you open the Property inspector, it displays all the file’s properties. The PDF pages are saved in HEIC format.

iAnalyse can import MIDI, MusicXML and MEI files. These files are transformed into a format that can be used as media for creating a Document. The audiovisual player uses the internal synthesizer in macOS or iPadOS to play the file. To import a music file: Use the File > Import menu and choose MIDI, MusicXML or MEI. Select one or more files, then confirm their addition to the Project. Each file can be displayed in the main view. If you open the Property inspector, it displays all the file’s properties. The supported formats are: MID, MEI, MusicXML, MXL

Data files allow you to add time-based values calculated or produced by other software to the Project. This data can then be displayed in graphical representations or used in certain calculations. The supported formats are: TXT, CSV

A data file generally contains a first column of time, then one or more columns of values. Example structure: 0.000000 0.00 0.011610 2.54 0.023220 6.84 0.034830 0.00 The first column indicates the time position. The following columns contain the values to represent.

Before confirming the import, check the data preview. Check in particular: Line ending format. The column separator. The unit of time (automatically detected). The number of series detected. An inconsistent preview often indicates a bad separator, incorrect time unit, or poorly formatted file. If there is a problem with the time unit indication, you can modify the automatic detection with the Advanced button.

You can import a segmentation when the temporal structure has been prepared in another tool. After importing, check the segment start times, end times and names in the timeline. An imported segmentation can then be modified like a segmentation created directly in iAnalyse. A segmentation file contains a first time column, then a column with segment labels. Example structure: 0.000000 Partie 1 10.011610 Partie 2 26 Partie 3 45.05 Partie 4 The structure of the data in the file must follow the example above. The supported formats are: TXT, CSV
Scala files allow you to add information related to scales or pitches. After import, check that the values correspond to the musical context of the Project. The supported format is: SCL
Once imported, the data can be selected in compatible representations: graph, gradient, fundamental frequency, matrix, chromagram or MFCCs depending on the file type.
Imported files are the sources used by the Documents and representations in the Project.

The browser displays the files available in the Project. Select a file to view its data and information. A single Project can contain several types of files: audio, video, image, PDF, MIDI, MusicXML, MEI, data, etc.
A file can only be deleted if it is no longer used in the Project. Use the Edit > Delete File menu.
If the Project was created on iOS, some video files may be linked. When opening the Project on macOS, iAnalyse offers to locate or import them.
Playback controls allow you to listen to or watch the active media while following the position in the timeline and Document.

Use the playback command in the toolbar to start or stop the active media. The playhead moves in the timeline and the Document's time elements update based on the current position. You can return to the beginning of the media or move directly to another position from the timeline: Use the button to start playback. Use the button to stop playback and return to the beginning. Move the pointer closer to the playhead: a selection strip appears. Click and drag to move the playhead. Use the → and ← shortcuts to move the playhead forward and backward. Jump duration can be set in preferences. Depending on the selected Document, other shortcuts are also available on the Keyboard shortcuts and gestures page.
The counter displays the time position of the playhead from the beginning. It also indicates the media used. Click on the counter to access the playback settings.

The playback settings allow you to modify: The volume. Playback speed without changing the pitch. The transposition of the pitch without changing the speed. By default, the transposition is by semitone, but it is possible to uncheck this option to do a continuous transposition. The inversion of the counter counting down the remaining time. The display of a countdown before the start of playback. You can display this view permanently by clicking on the area at the top above the text and then dragging it to detach it.

In the timeline, it is possible to select a playback range by clicking and dragging on the timeline ruler. This range is then played in a loop and the symbol appears next to the counter in the toolbar: Click and drag on the time ruler to draw the area to loop. Click and release to cancel loop playback.
The timeline displays the temporal organization of the Project. It is used to monitor playback, navigate media, move annotations, display markers and work with segmentations.

The timeline is read from left to right. The current position is indicated by the playhead. A graduated ruler indicates time positions in minutes:seconds. Annotations, markers, segmentations, and temporal representations are displayed in the timeline. You can show or hide the timeline with the toolbar button ().

Click the time ruler to place the playhead at a specific position. You can also drag it to browse the media. When playback is active, the playhead advances automatically. Items synced with time update in the main view.

The zoom slider at the bottom left allows you to work at different scales: Zoom out to see the entire Project. Zoom in to precisely adjust an annotation, a marker or the segment of a segmentation. To the right of the zoom slider, you find different controls: : cancels zoom to view the entire timeline. : activates playhead tracking; it always remains visible while the media is playing. : activates timeline scrolling; the playhead always remains in the center. : for Video Documents, divides the timeline into two parts. : displays the segmentation in the timeline. : opens the timeline display options. This panel provides access to the most common options. To view all options, use the Property inspector. : Opens the timeline Property inspector.

The timeline allows you to select time elements. Once an element is selected, you can adjust its position, duration or properties from the inspector. But you can also adjust these temporal properties in the timeline. For example, for annotations: Select the annotation in the main view. In the timeline, the annotation occupies the entire height. Move the pointer to the beginning, end or middle of the annotation. A colored band appears; you can click and drag. If the selection strips do not appear or are not active, increase the zoom slider a little.

This page brings together the most common problems and the first steps to try before making major changes to a Project.

If iAnalyse can no longer find media, check that the file has not been moved, renamed, or deleted. Use the location command provided to indicate its new location. If the Project must be shared, choose a strategy or format that copies the necessary media into the Project.

A Project can become large when it contains videos, copied media, high definition images or numerous calculations. Delete unused files where possible using the Edit > Delete Unused Files menu. On iPadOS, also check the Project strategy.

If a file doesn't import, check its format, extension, and contents. For data files, check the column separator, time unit, and value structure. Try importing a simple file to check if the problem is with the format or the file itself.

If an export fails, try a smaller size or more compatible format first. High-resolution video exports can take a long time and take up a lot of disk space. Also check that the Project is saved and that the export location is accessible. You can also export to the computer’s or tablet’s local storage, rather than an external drive or cloud storage.

Always keep a copy of the original Project before opening it in iAnalyse 6. After import, check the media, annotations, representations and segmentations. Imported Slideshow Documents may look different. This is expected; allow time to adjust them.
To improve responsiveness, reduce the elements displayed simultaneously, hide unnecessary layers, close unnecessary views, and avoid heavy representations during editing.

If the application suddenly closes when opening a Project located in the cloud, verify that the synchronization is complete. This issue can occur when you open a Project that has just been edited on another device, or when you reopen a Project on the same device without waiting for syncing to complete. Avoid opening the same file on macOS and iPadOS at the same time.

documents.t: Audio filters allow you to filter the frequencies of an imported file in order to create a new file. This function is useful for: Listening to a file with selected frequency bands filtered. Amplifying frequency bands. Creating representations centered on one or more frequency bands.

Select an audio or video file in the browser. Use the File > New > Audio Filter menu. A new tool appears in the browser with the icon . Video files must have an audio track to be selected to create an audio filter.

Use the button on the toolbar to add a filter. The filters appear in the form of transparent rectangles on the spectrogram. Adjust the filter position and its properties with the inspector. Click the Filtered button at the bottom of the timeline. The calculation of the filtered file is then carried out. Click the playback controls to listen to the filtered file. If you change a filter property, playback switches to Original at the bottom of the timeline. You must then click on the Filtered button to calculate the filtered file again. You can add as many filters as you want. You can also export the filtered file by clicking the Export button at the bottom of the timeline. The file is then added to the browser. If your file contains harmonic musical instruments, it is best to switch the spectrogram to logarithmic by clicking the button at the bottom right of the timeline and selecting Spectrogram > Type > Logarithmic.
After selecting the tool, display the Property inspector with the button on the toolbar. The inspector properties are organized into 2 parts.

The Name of the tool. The Color of the filters. The Opacity of the filters. Display of Information on filters. The Mode: Pass (default): only allows frequencies under the filters to pass. Rejection: lets all frequencies pass except those under the filters. Out-of-Band Gain manages the level in dB outside the filters.
The Start time position of the filter. The End time position of the filter. The High Frequency of the filter in Hz. The Low Frequency of the filter in Hz. The Gain of the filter in dB.
